The Kitchen

Chef Tunde Adewale

A Lagos boy who cooked his way through London and Copenhagen — and came home to cook over fire.

The Story

From his grandmother's kitchen to an open flame.

Tunde Adewale grew up watching his grandmother slow-cook over wood in Ibadan. He trained at Le Cordon Bleu London, then spent six years in the kitchens of Copenhagen's two-star fire restaurants — learning the discipline of flame, ash and smoke.

In 2019 he returned to Lagos and opened EMBER & OAK: a room built around a single oak-fired hearth, where the techniques of Nordic fire cooking meet the ingredients and memory of home.

The Philosophy

Slow heat, honest ingredients.

Everything that leaves this kitchen has met fire. We butcher in-house, cure our own meats, ferment our peppers, and bake bread over embers each morning.

Our suppliers are friends — fishers from Ibeno, herders from the north, market women whose families we have known for years. Real food has a postcode, and ours is Lagos.
